about.title: Yreka Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone suddenly changes the shape of a small town. In Yreka, where fewer than 8,000 people live along the I-5 corridor in Siskiyou County, a death caused by another's carelessness is rarely private; neighbors, coworkers and the shops along S Main Street all feel it. Public collision records show Yreka recorded 9 injury collisions and 13 people hurt in 2025, with no traffic fatalities that year. That is welcome news, but wrongful death claims in this area do not come only from crashes. Long-haul trucking on Interstate 5, ranch and timber work, medical care that may require a drive to a distant hospital, and everyday travel on Rt 3 can each lead to a loss that was preventable. California law lets a surviving spouse, domestic partner or child, and in some cases other dependents, bring a civil claim for funeral costs, lost financial support and the loss of love and guidance. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Yreka families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can confirm where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Getting an early conversation on the calendar protects your options.

items.title: No Fee Unless There Is a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, and LawProactive itself never charges you. Your family can ask questions about funeral costs, lost support and loss of companionship without worrying about a bill.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on Interstate 5 near Yreka, but the other driver was from out of state. Can we still bring a claim here?
items.answer: In most cases, yes. A wrongful death claim is generally brought where the incident happened or where the responsible party can be reached, and a death on I-5 in Siskiyou County typically falls under California law. An attorney can sort out the jurisdiction details and deal with an out-of-state insurer on your behalf.

items.question: The district attorney is already pursuing charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: A criminal case and a wrongful death claim are separate. The criminal matter is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while the civil claim belongs to the family and addresses losses such as funeral expenses, lost income and the loss of guidance and companionship. One does not replace the other, and a criminal outcome does not decide the civil claim.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Siskiyou County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a city, county or state agency may share responsibility, a formal claim usually has to be presented much sooner, often within six months. Because those timelines can overlap with grief and estate matters, it helps to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.
